results.reason: Issue 3 contrasts Sched. §1.1 (date shipped from Supplier's plant) with MSA §1.3 (delivery at Rochester). It explains that a shipment sent on time but arriving late counts as on time, which undercuts the §5.2 lateness remedies. It also covers risk of loss in transit and the payment trigger starting at shipment.
The fix adds an order-of-precedence clause and conforms the Schedule's Delivery Date definition to MSA §1.3 (delivery at Rochester).

Issue 1 identifies MSA §4.3's 'all housings and similar components worldwide' and contrasts it with Term Sheet §§3.1–3.3 (Series 7, U.S. only). It explains the lock-in and the sourcing bar and recommends narrowing to Series 7 in the U.S. Non-U.S. plants are not named, but the worldwide scope and the bar on other sourcing are covered.

Issue 5.1 flags MSA §15.2: Supplier may assign without consent while Customer needs consent. It notes the risk of a competing assignee holding Harlow's Specifications under the exclusivity lock-in. It recommends mutual consent, or at minimum no competitors and a change-of-control termination right.

Issue 2 explains that Amendment §2.1/§2.2 restates §11.2 to exclude only willful misconduct, subjecting gross negligence and the IP indemnity to the cap. It recommends restoring the original §11.2(a)–(c).
The memo states the cap is fees paid in the prior 12 months (§11.1). It states the original §11.2 excluded gross negligence, willful misconduct and the IP indemnity (§10.1).
Term Sheet §§3.1–3.3 (Series 7 Housings only, United States) is expressly used as the baseline for comparison with MSA §4.3.

The memo states New York law governs (MSA §16.1) and includes a detailed assumptions and open-facts section. It cites no cases. The UCC citations are real sections, not invented, and are flagged as to be confirmed. The NY public-policy point is flagged as unresearched.
The memo is addressed to the partner and gives each issue with Where / Why it matters / Fix. Issues are ordered by importance, and there are assumptions/facts-needed and talking-points sections.

The Term Sheet is used as evidence of intent and as leverage, not treated as defective. The 3-year term and renewal are noted as consistent with the Term Sheet. The 45-day payment term is expressly noted as not a departure. The payment concern is tied only to the Delivery Date conflict.

Section attributions for exclusivity (§4.3), assignment (§15.2) and the cap provisions are accurate, and party benefit is correctly described. Legal authority beyond the documents (the UCC and the NY gross-negligence policy) is flagged as needing verification.
